messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE — Severity 2 — elevated 5xx and high tail latency detected for inference-redwood-prod (prod-us-west). alert id: A-1782000000. Paging @alice @helen. link: https://internal.redwood/incidents/1782000000

alice: I'm up. seeing 503 spikes from the runtime pool 3 (gpu-23). starting timeline analysis. any recent deploys?

helen: handoff note — I just finished the 02:00 maintenance windows, no runtime deploys from me, only autoscaler bump. passing to @alice.

incident-bot: Incident created by oncall-bot at 1782000000. Status: investigating. Attach: log-sampling-note:enabled=false

bob: quick snapshot from the runtime logs — a bunch of kv-cache miss storms followed by OOM-ish rejection from the tokenizer pool. copy paste of tail: 
```
[1782000012] ERROR runtime: request handler failed: downstream err=503 code=E_RUNTIME_OVERCAPACITY trace=tx-0a12
[1782000012] WARN runtime.batch: kv-cache miss rate 87% (expected <5%) pool=gpu-23
[1782000013] ERROR tokenizer: allocate failed: no mem available
```

carla: Can someone confirm if we changed log sampling on the runtime logging pipeline? I recall a change to drop verbose logs for batcher last week.

greg: checking observability — dashboards are showing normal ingestion but traces look sampled at 0.1 for runtime service. I can't find kernel-selection logs at all for this window. Possible sampling rule applied incorrectly.

derek: hypothesis: autoscaler bumped new nodes without warming caches -> cache miss spike -> higher latency -> requests queue -> runtime rejects. Also maybe a recent kernel selection fallback added a hot path.

alice: timeline so far (I'll keep updating):
- 1781999800 (~ -200s): autoscaler scale-up triggered for prod-us-west due to throughput spike.
- 1781999900: new runtime instances booted (gpu-21..gpu-24).
- 1782000005: first 503s observed, kv-cache miss spike.
- 1782000015: 503 rate climbs to 30% for 30s.

helen: customer impact: some Dedicated customers reported timeouts, support queue increased. @eva can you surface top 3 customers affected?

eva: already collecting — initial list: cust-emerald, cust-halo, cust-borealis. I pinged CS; they're templating notices. ETA for status update to customers 10m.

bob: more logs — I'm seeing truncation on request_id for some entries (maybe logger formatter). that makes correlating traces harder. snippet: 
```
[1782000020] INFO request: id=tx-???? user=internal svc=inference runtime=handler
```

carla: confirmed — we reverted a JSON size increase last month which changed some log fields; someone also toggled 'reduce-trace-ids' in prod logging rules on 1781900000. That might be why request ids are masked.

alice: immediate mitigations: 1) pause autoscaler (carla?) 2) increase runtime log sampling for full traces (greg) 3) fail-open tokenization path to avoid allocation failure (bob). executing now.

carla: pausing autoscaler now (manual scale lock). cpu/autoscale policy set to paused.

greg: bumping trace sampling to 1.0 for service=redwood-runtime for timeframe 1781999800..1782000600. running query to backfill missing traces. query: 
```
index=logs service=redwood-runtime | where timestamp >= 1781999800 and level in (ERROR, WARN)
```

bob: applied config change: tokenizer fallbacks -> fail-open true. monitoring for reduced allocation errors.

derek: running ad-hoc eval to see if kernel-selection fallback changed: 
```
SELECT kernel_variant, count(*) FROM kernel_logs WHERE ts between 1781999800 and 1782000200 GROUP BY kernel_variant;
```
result: fallback_variant_x increased from 2% -> 65% during spike. suggests new kernel selection heuristics are misrouting.

alice: observability gap notes (to include in RCA):
- missing request_id field on many log lines (logger config mismatch).
- trace sampling set to 0.1 for runtime (should be 1.0 on high-sev).
- dashboard metric for kv-cache miss rate aggregates per-host but was set to 5m resolution — too coarse to catch rapid miss storms.
- kernel-selection traces are not emitted at debug level due to a separate env toggle.

helen: good list. assigning owners: kernel selection logs -> @derek, request_id/logger -> @carla, dashboards -> @greg, customer comms -> @eva.

bob: sharing a log bundle for correlation (redacted): https://artifacts.redwood/logs/1782000000/bundle.tgz

alice: next steps (in-incident RCA coordination):
- gather full logs + traces (greg)
- reconstruct per-request timeline for 50 failed requests (bob + derek)
- if kernel heuristics confirmed, rollback kernel selector change (carla)
- update dashboards and sampling rules to avoid blind spots (greg)
- draft customer impact summary (eva)

incident-bot: Action items recorded. Incident severity remains S2. Update channel when mitigation completes.

carla: I see a recent change to kernel-selector rollout (canary) deployed 2 hours ago, flagged 25% traffic. I'm rolling that canary to 0% now.

derek: while that rollback is happening, I'm extracting a few full traces from the newly changed nodes to validate behavior. attaching trace ids: tx-0a12, tx-0b34, tx-0c56.

bob: quick note — some logs show truncated stack traces because sampling compaction ran for batcher. need to disable compaction for error-level logs. filing patch.

alice: status update 1782000300: after canary -> 0% and tokenizer fail-open, 503 rate dropped to 3% and tail latency improving. still monitoring for recurrence.

helen: thanks team. once stabilized, let's capture a clean timeline and call a short RCA sync. I expect to move to postmortem planning in ~2h.

eva: customer update: initial notice sent to affected accounts. CS will follow-up with mitigation summary in 30m.

greg: observability fixes I'll do in parallel: restore request_id emission, increase dashboard resolution to 30s for kv-cache miss, and make kernel-selection logs emitted at INFO for 1h window.

alice: wrapping up thread: please paste any extra logs/hypotheses here. I'll create a doc and invite owners. good work everyone. :thumbsup:
